approach: Root cause: nothing makes the producer measure a new or tightened refusal rule against past accepted readings while it works. The replay (`replay_stage`, run/mod.rs:1743, one call at mod.rs:1714) runs once after the producer finishes, as a verification hold. The producer loop (run/producer.rs `producer_loop`) never sees the newly refused list or the share. The fix is in `producer_loop`. After each parsed report whose change list touches `crates/` or the Cargo files, a new `loop_replay` builds the candidate commit with `build_candidate`, takes a build slot, and runs the existing replay code (`replay_cases`, `replay`, `replay_checkers`) with the hold's limit: `replay_limit_percent(declared)`, which is `REPLAY_HOLD_PERCENT` (10) or the declared share plus 5. A held replay (ids, measured percent, limit) joins the one existing send-back (`PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS`); if still held on the last pass it goes into `report_gaps`. Cost, answering round-1 findings 1 and 2: the post-hoc replay already builds both sides for every job that has history, with no path gate (mod.rs:1764-1798). So the last in-loop result is carried (`LoopReplay`: candidate tree, case ids, run) through `Reported` and `Built` to `replay_run`. When the admitted candidate has the same tree (`Git::tree_of`) and the same case ids, and the run was measured, the hold reuses it and builds nothing more. A job that is not sent back therefore pays no more builds than today, and a sent-back job pays one more pair. The in-loop builds take a `Class::Producer` build slot and build into that slot's warm target directory, which is cleaned afterwards the way `SnapExec` does. The post-hoc hold, verify.rs's blocker and the Replay record stay as the backstop. An unrunnable replay, an empty history, a short disk or a slot wait prints `replay     in the loop: no replay: <reason>`, is never a pass and never a send-back. No refusal rule, record, config key or prompt file is added.

decisions.choice: Run the replay inside `producer_loop` after every parsed producer report whose change list touches `crates/` or Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock, and feed the result into the one existing send-back.
decisions.reason: The cause is that the producer never sees the measurement while it can still act on it. The send-back already returns per-pass problems in the same work directory, so a new problem kind needs no new retry mechanism and no extra model call.

rejected.option: Move `replay_stage` out of `check_and_verify` into the loop
rejected.why: The hold is the backstop for a producer that does not fix it and for jobs resumed from a kept candidate, which skip the producer loop. verify.rs's blocker and the Replay record are out of scope.

rejected.option: A second send-back or new retry loop for the replay
rejected.why: It changes `PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS` semantics and cost; the brief asks for the existing retry budget.
That is one instance of a rule; the class is that no rule is measured while the producer works. It is out of scope.

decisions.choice: Keep the broad path gate (`touches_reading_rules`: any path under `crates/`, Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock) and state its purpose honestly: a docs-only change cannot alter compiled reading rules, so it is never sent back and never replayed in the loop. The gate is not the cost control; reuse is.
decisions.reason: The critic's count (866 `crates/` path lines in 200 commits of HISTORY.txt, not re-measured by me) shows the gate matches almost every code job. That is acceptable because `replay_run` has no path gate today (mod.rs:1764-1798): every job with history already builds both sides after the producer. With reuse, a job that is not sent back adds no builds.

rejected.option: Narrow the gate to the reading-rule modules and the CLI subcommand (round-1 option d)
rejected.why: `check-reading` links athena-core and its dependencies; a path list for what it compiles would drift and miss a helper change, which is the failure class.

rejected.option: Replay on every pass of every job
rejected.why: Docs-only jobs cannot change the rules; replaying them would add builds for nothing.

rejected.option: Detect a new rule by parsing the diff for `step!(check_`
rejected.why: Misses a tightened keyword table or helper change.

decisions.choice: Reuse the last in-loop measurement in the post-hoc hold (round-1 option c). `Reported` and `Built` carry `Option<LoopReplay { tree, cases: Vec<JobId>, run }>`. `replay_run` still first returns `no replay: a check failed` when a check failed. It then reuses the run only if `run.no_replay` is None, `Git::tree_of(candidate)` equals `tree`, and the case ids from a fresh `replay_cases` equal `cases`. Otherwise it measures as today. Resumed jobs (Built at mod.rs:602) carry None.
decisions.reason: Same base, same tree and same corpus give the same answer, so reuse changes cost and not the verdict. `candidate_tree` is a function of the base and the change list (candidate.rs:98-110), so the in-loop tree equals the admitted tree when the work is unchanged.

rejected.option: Build the base checker once per job and cache the binary (option a)
rejected.why: Saves one build only on the rare sent-back path. It needs a second code path through `replay_checkers`. Reuse removes the whole post-hoc pair instead.
The slot's warm target directory already does this and is bounded by `slot_max_gb`; a job-local one would add disk.

decisions.choice: The in-loop builds run in a `Class::Producer` slot from `SlotQueue::from_config(&self.state, &pipeline)`, built into `state.slot_target(slot.index())` prepared by `prepare_slot_target(index, slot_max_gb * GB)`. Afterwards `slots::clean_workspace_output(<candidate tree>, <target>)` runs, with `reset_slot_target` on failure, as `SnapExec::clean_slot_target` does (checks.rs:188-202). The slot is held only across the two builds. `replay_checkers` gains a `target` parameter; the post-hoc call passes `dir.join("target")` as now. A `SlotWait` becomes `no replay: no build slot was free within build_wait_s`. A kill-switch error from the stop closure propagates.
decisions.reason: agent-and-build-slots.md budgets disk and memory per concurrent build, and the in-loop builds overlap the producer's build directory. A slot makes them count, and the warm target removes the cold third-party rebuild. Only `Class::Check` is requested today (slots.rs header), so `Class::Producer` is the class the module already defines for this.

rejected.option: No slot; state the memory cost as an estimate
rejected.why: Two overlapping cargo builds per job would exceed the per-build disk budget the slot design depends on.

rejected.option: Hold the job on a slot wait, as the checks do
rejected.why: The in-loop replay is an advisory early signal and the post-hoc hold is the backstop, so a wait must not stop the job.

decisions.choice: Every in-loop UI line starts `replay     in the loop: `. A measurement reads `N of M accepted readings newly refused (P%, limit L%)` and a skip reads `no replay: <reason>`. It is printed before the later `checks` line.
decisions.reason: The post-hoc stage already prints `replay     no replay: ...` for the same reasons (mod.rs:1752), so tests on the unprefixed text pass on the base tree. A distinct prefix lets tests assert the in-loop check ran, and where.

risks.risk: Cost: the in-loop replay builds `athena` twice per gated pass, and the gate on `crates/` matches most code jobs.
risks.mitigation: The cost claim is now by mechanism, not by the gate. The post-hoc replay already builds a pair for every job with history (mod.rs:1764-1798). The in-loop result is reused by the hold for the same tree and corpus, so a job that is not sent back adds zero builds and a sent-back job adds one pair (an estimate: two workspace builds, with third-party crates warm in the slot's target). The measurement rule is the same on both paths. A test counts candidate-checker calls.

risks.risk: Reuse could hide a changed candidate or a corpus that moved, weakening the backstop.
risks.mitigation: Reuse is allowed only when the in-loop run was measured, `Git::tree_of(candidate)` equals the in-loop tree, and the fresh `replay_cases` ids equal the stored ones; any difference measures again as today. `candidate_tree` depends only on the base and the change list (candidate.rs:98-110). The test for each mismatch is the `loop_replay_covers_only_the_same_tree_and_cases` unit test.

risks.risk: Slot contention: the in-loop build could wait behind other jobs, or block the producer's later checks.
risks.mitigation: A `Class::Producer` slot is held only across the two builds and released before the replay runs and before the checks ask for a `Class::Check` slot. A `SlotWait` becomes `no replay: no build slot...` and the post-hoc hold still runs. The kill-switch error propagates. The warm target is cleaned with `clean_workspace_output`, falling back to `reset_slot_target`. If `prepare_slot_target` fails, a warning prints and the build uses `dir/target`, cold.

risks.risk: Disk: the builds overlap the producer's build directory, which is still on disk.
risks.mitigation: The disk gate runs before the builds and short space becomes `no replay: free disk space is low` (the post-hoc stage and checks hold as before). Only one slot's warm directory is used, bounded by `slot_max_gb`.

risks.risk: A producer that cannot reduce the share wastes its one send-back, and a job that would be rejected anyway costs a second producer run.
risks.mitigation: The path gate keeps docs-only jobs out. The combined send-back stays within `PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS` (1). The post-hoc hold is unchanged, so an unfixable job is still rejected there.

risks.risk: The send-back list could be long or quote old request text.
risks.mitigation: Reasons are capped by `REPLAY_BRIEF_REASON_CHARS` (200) and the list by `REPLAY_BRIEF_MAX_LISTED` (20) with an 'and N more' line. The send-back states which limit applied.

risks.risk: `build_candidate` inside the loop writes a dangling commit and hashes blobs into the user's repository on each pass.
risks.mitigation: `build_candidate` writes only an unreferenced commit, the same kind `candidate_stage` makes. The admitted commit is still built by `candidate_stage`, and the test asserts the final candidate and `replay.json`.

risks.risk: The new text breaks a pinned test outside the deliverables (run_pin_tests.rs) or a producer-brief test.
risks.mitigation: The wrapper delegates with None and its text is unchanged then. With a replay, the intro keeps the pinned phrases word for word and only a sentence is added in front. The full suite is run in the last step.

The job ends `OutcomeState::Landed` and `replay.json` has 0 newly refused. In the reuse test one passing pass makes the candidate closure run exactly 10 times (the in-loop pass only; the hold reuses it), and the recorded Replay equals the in-loop run.
demonstrations.fails_without: On the base tree the producer runs once and its prompt has no `## Sent back`, and no `replay     in the loop:` line exists. The post-hoc hold then rejects the job with 3 of 10 newly refused. The prompt-count, brief-content, UI-line and Landed assertions all fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `Athena::go` (via the existing `finished_job` helper), reaching `produce_and_verify`, `producer_loop`, the new `loop_replay` and, for the reuse test, `replay_run`. Guards: the change list must touch a path under `crates/`, and the history must be non-empty. Fixture `seed_accepted_jobs(&athena, 10, 3)` (exists, tests.rs:1417) seeds 3 marked readings of 10. Fake: `crate::replay_seam::install(real_rules(), candidate)` (exists, lib.rs:174), where the candidate closure refuses the marker title only while a shared `Arc<AtomicUsize>` producer-run counter is below 2 and bumps a second call counter. `athena_with` (exists, tests.rs:187) takes a script wrapping `base_script` that bumps the counter on `Role::Producer`, edits `crates/demo/src/lib.rs` and README.md, and records each `user_prompt`. The closures hold only counters; the replay, limit, slot and send-back text are production code. The seam is read after the slot is taken, so the production slot path runs. The tests are added by plan step 8.

demonstrations.method: A unit test on the limit and boundary, plus three run tests through `Athena::go`.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core replay_limit_is_declared_share_plus_five && cargo test -p athena-core in_loop_replay_exactly_at_the_default_limit && cargo test -p athena-core an_unrunnable_replay_says_no_replay_in_the_loop && cargo test -p athena-core an_in_loop_replay_waits_for_a_build_slot
demonstrations.observes: `replay_limit_percent(None)` is 10 and `Some(20)` is 25. With total 50, 5 newly refused and no declared share is not held and 6 is; with declared 20 and total 20, 5 is not held and 6 is. `replay()` over closure checkers shows the same boundary. Run test: 1 of 10 marked (10%) gives one prompt, no `## Sent back`, and the line `(10%, limit 10%)`; 2 of 10 (20%) gives a second prompt naming `20%` and the limit. Unrunnable test: it calls `seed_accepted_jobs` first, so the empty-history reason is not reached. With no seam and the fake driver, a UI line `replay     in the loop: no replay: the driver is a fake, so nothing is built` appears before the `checks` line. No `in the loop: 0 of` line appears, there is one producer prompt, and the post-hoc `replay.no_replay` is Some. Slot test: config `[drain.pipeline] build_wait_s = 1`, a test-held slot via `SlotQueue::try_acquire`, the seam installed and history seeded. The line is `replay     in the loop: no replay: no build slot was free within build_wait_s`, one producer prompt, and `go` returns a `SlotWait` error from the checks, as in `a_check_that_waits_past_build_wait_s_holds_the_job` (tests.rs:2759).
demonstrations.fails_without: The unit test does not compile without `replay_limit_percent`. In the 20% run test the base tree sees one producer prompt, so the second-prompt assertion fails. The unrunnable test asserts a line starting `replay     in the loop: no replay:`, which the base tree never prints (it prints only the unprefixed post-hoc line). The slot test asserts that line carries `no build slot` while the only slot is held; the base tree prints none, and an in-loop replay that skipped the slot would measure instead.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points `replay_is_held`, `replay_limit_percent`, `replay` (reading.rs) and `Athena::go`. Fakes: closure `ReadingChecker`s in the unit test; `seed_accepted_jobs`; `replay_seam::install` with `real_rules()`; `repo_with_config`, `slot_queue` and `take_slot_soon` (exist, tests.rs:2346-2380); `Lines` UI (tests.rs:167). The seam is deliberately not installed in the unrunnable test; the fake driver's own skip in `replay_checkers` (mod.rs:1818) makes it unrunnable. `replay_limit_percent` is added by step 1; `loop_replay` and its slot by step 5; the tests by steps 1 and 8.

demonstrations.method: Two run tests through `Athena::go` plus a pure unit test of the path gate.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core a_job_whose_change_touches_no_reading_rule && cargo test -p athena-core an_empty_history_in_the_loop && cargo test -p athena-core touches_reading_rules
demonstrations.observes: (a) With the seam installed over 3 of 10 marked and the default README-only `base_script`, there is one producer prompt and no line containing `in the loop`; the post-hoc hold still rejects the job. (b) With no seeded jobs and a producer editing a `crates/` file, the line `replay     in the loop: no replay: no accepted readings in the history` (`NO_HISTORY_REASON`) appears before the `checks` line. There is one producer prompt and no `in the loop: 0 of 0` line. The post-hoc `replay.no_replay` equals `no replay: no accepted readings in the history`, so it is not success. Unit test: `README.md` false, `docs/x.md` false, `crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs` true, `Cargo.lock` true, empty list false.
demonstrations.fails_without: (a) If the loop replayed every change, the README-only run would print an in-loop line and take a second prompt. (b) The base tree prints no `in the loop` line, so the line assertion fails; if an empty corpus counted as a pass, a `0 of 0` in-loop line or a missing `no replay` would fail it. The unit test fails if the gate is missing or wrong.
demonstrations.seam: Entry point `Athena::go`; fixtures `seed_accepted_jobs`, `replay_seam::install`, `Lines` and `athena_with` (all exist). `touches_reading_rules` is a pure function added by step 1; the run tests are added by step 8.

demonstrations.method: Read the docs diff and run the briefs test that the producer brief names the replay and its limit.
demonstrations.command: git diff -- docs/architecture.md CHANGELOG.md crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs && cargo test -p athena-context producer_brief_tells_the_producer_the_replay_is_checked_while_it_works
demonstrations.observes: Both docs describe the replay as a check inside the producer loop. They give the limit (`REPLAY_HOLD_PERCENT`, or the declared share plus 5), the `crates/`/Cargo gate, the build slot, the single shared send-back, and `no replay: <reason>` never being a pass. They state that the same-tree measurement is reused by the hold, and that the post-hoc verification hold stays as the backstop. The CHANGELOG entry is under [Unreleased]. The briefs test asserts the producer brief mentions the in-loop replay and its limit.
demonstrations.fails_without: The briefs.rs test fails on the base tree because the producer brief has no replay section.
demonstrations.seam: `producer_brief` (exists, briefs.rs) is called directly by the test; no fake. The section and test are added by step 2.

demonstrations.method: Run the three repository checks from the repository root.
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
demonstrations.observes: All three exit 0, including every new test from criteria 2 to 4, the existing replay tests, the run_pin_tests send-back tests, the briefs.rs tests and `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus`. The refusal corpus is unaffected because no `step!(check_` line is added (the extractor reads only those lines); I read the test names `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` and `no_check_bypasses_refusing_check` and cite no result.
demonstrations.fails_without: `cargo test --locked` fails on the base tree plus the new tests alone, because they call functions that do not exist. It also fails if the change breaks an existing test, for example a run_pin_tests send-back test, a prompt-count test or the replay tests at tests.rs:1488, 1605, 1667. Clippy fails on an unused import or dead wrapper; fmt fails on unformatted code.
demonstrations.seam: The cargo commands themselves, on the producer's tree at the repository root; no fake. The tests they run use existing seams (`Athena::go`, `athena_with`, `seed_accepted_jobs`, `replay_seam::install`, `Lines`, `slot_queue`).
